item.title: A Plant-Powered Fundraising Opportunity for FFA Chapters This Spring
item.description: FFA chapters across the country have a new opportunity to grow their spring fundraisers—literally—thanks to an exciting new partnership between Seminis and Ball Seed. The Plant-Powered Fundraiser Program gives FFA chapters discounted access to professional-grade vegetable seeds, allowing students to raise funds while gaining valuable, hands-on growing experience. It’s a program designed to connect agriculture education, entrepreneurship, and community involvement all in one planting season.

item.title: Kansas Ranchers Represent at the National Western Stock Show
item.description: The world of agriculture is on full display just five minutes from downtown Denver this time of year, as the National Western Stock Show celebrates a major milestone. The iconic event officially kicked off its 120th year, drawing ranchers, exhibitors, and livestock enthusiasts from across the country—including many from Kansas.

item.title: Preparing Students for a Successful Return to the Farm
item.description: For many students pursuing degrees in agriculture, college is not an exit from the farm — it’s a step toward returning home better prepared than ever.

item.title: Kansas Leads Nation in Avian Influenza Cases, Officials Say Relief May Be in Sight
item.description: Kansas is currently facing the most severe outbreak of highly pathogenic avian influenza in the nation, according to the USDA. The virus has heavily impacted poultry across the state, placing Kansas at the top of the national map for confirmed cases over the last 30 days.

item.title: From Kansas Roots to the National Stage: Lindy McMillen’s Farm Bureau Journey
item.description: For many young people in agriculture, finding a place where their voice truly matters can be transformative. For Lindy McMillen, that journey started in high school—and led all the way to the national stage.

item.title: Kansas Soybean Celebration Highlights Policy, Leadership and Clean Fuel Opportunities for 2026
item.description: The start of a new year often brings reflection on the challenges and victories of the past 12 months — and renewed focus on the road ahead. That spirit was on full display at the Kansas Soybean Celebration, where growers gathered to look ahead at policy priorities, leadership development, and new market opportunities.

item.title: Positioning for Profit: Fertilizer Efficiency with AgroLiquid
item.description: As Kansas farmers wrap up the 2025 growing season and begin planning for 2026, there’s a renewed sense of cautious optimism across the country. After several challenging years, moisture levels heading into winter are offering something many producers haven’t had in a while — a solid foundation.

item.title: John Deere Introduces New Gator Technology for Boundary Mapping at Commodity Classic
item.description: New technology coming to the John Deere Gator could soon make it easier and more affordable for farmers to map field boundaries and utilize precision agriculture tools. At this year’s Commodity Classic, John Deere showcased new technology options for its Gator utility vehicles that will allow producers to integrate precision technology into an open-station Gator for the first time.

item.title: DeKalb Brings New Seed Technology and Yield Potential to Producers
item.description: Advancements in seed technology continue to play a major role in helping farmers protect their crops and maximize yields. During a recent conversation, I spoke with Matt Strubhart of DeKalb about what sets the company’s corn hybrids apart and the innovations the brand is bringing to producers across the region.DeKalb continues to focus on providing a strong genetic portfolio designed to perform across a wide range of environments. item.title: Farm Machinery Market Reset: What Low Commodity Prices Mean for Equipment Financing in 2026
item.description: Agriculture has faced several challenging years as producers navigate fluctuating markets and lower commodity prices. As the industry moves into 2026, many are beginning to see signs of stabilization in the farm machinery market.

item.title: BASF Introduces New Fungicide “Zorina” to Combat White Mold in Key Crops
item.description: As farmers continue to face challenges from persistent crop diseases, new tools are entering the market to help protect yields. Representatives from BASF are highlighting their latest fungicide innovation—Zorina—and what it could mean for producers across the region.

item.title: BASF Highlights Corn Opportunities, Carbon Markets, and Data Tools at Commodity Classic
item.description: At Commodity Classic, Brady Spangenberg with BASF shared insight into what’s ahead for farmers in 2026. From corn market opportunities to sustainability practices and digital tools, several key themes are shaping conversations across agriculture this year.

item.title: Kansas Farmers Prepare for Planting Season with Key Agronomic Considerations
item.description: As planting season approaches across Kansas, farmers are beginning to make critical decisions that can impact crop success for the entire year. From soil conditions to seed selection, preparation is key to getting crops off to a strong start.

item.title: Marshall Highlights Biofuel Growth, Farmer Benefits, and Push for Year-Round E15
item.description: Kansas agriculture continues to see opportunities in the growing biofuels industry, and U.S. Senator Roger Marshall says recent policy moves are helping drive demand for both corn and soybeans. Speaking during a visit to Western Plains Energy in Oakley, Kansas, Marshall pointed to strong export numbers as a sign of momentum in the industry.
